root_cause.text: In `drivers/target/target_core_configfs.c`, `target_tg_pt_gp_members_show()` used the raw `snprintf()` return value as the copy length from a 256-byte stack buffer without bounding it, so long iSCSI/fabric WWN names could make `cur_len` exceed the buffer and cause an out-of-bounds stack read into sysfs output.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (cur_len > TG_PT_GROUP_NAME_BUF || (cur_len + len) > PAGE_SIZE)` before the `memcpy()` path, and the CVE description states the missing check allowed `memcpy()` to read past the stack buffer because `snprintf()` “returns the length the output would have had,” which can be larger than 256 bytes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an additional bounds check to prevent overflowing the target portal group name buffer while formatting membership output.
intent_record.what: The bounds check in `target_tg_pt_gp_members_show()` was changed from `if ((cur_len + len) > PAGE_SIZE)` to `if (cur_len > TG_PT_GROUP_NAME_BUF || (cur_len + len) > PAGE_SIZE)`, adding an explicit upper-limit check against `TG_PT_GROUP_NAME_BUF` before continuing.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now stops building the members string not only when the overall page buffer would overflow, but also when the current group-name buffer length exceeds the dedicated `TG_PT_GROUP_NAME_BUF` limit. This prevents writing or formatting member names beyond the intended per-name buffer boundary and avoids potential overflow or malformed output.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this file version. In the relevant members-show functions, the code either bounds the output with PAGE_SIZE or uses a buffer copy length derived from a bounded snprintf into a local buffer. For example, `target_core_alua_lu_gp_show_attr_members()` does `cur_len = snprintf(buf, LU_GROUP_NAME_BUF, "%s/%s\n", ...)`, then checks `if ((cur_len + len) > PAGE_SIZE) { ... break; }`, and only then `memcpy(page+len, buf, cur_len);`. This prevents the raw snprintf return value from being used to overrun the destination page buffer in the way described. The snippet does not show the later `target_tg_pt_gp_members_show()` bug at all, so the vulnerable statement is absent here.
